metadata.description: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for the Seed action library. scripts/seed/seed_action_library.js reads this file and computes points from effort/frequency/impact at seed time -- it no longer carries an inline action array. Every shipping action lives here.
metadata.methodology: Values cross-referenced from 2-3 tier-1 sources minimum. Conservative estimates used when sources disagree.

grid_factors.note: Superseded the retired 386 g CO2/kWh on 2026-08-02 (decision E1). Regional factors are a separate open question -- see Plan/PDR_GRID_REGIONALISATION.md.

actions.description_en: Choose a plant-based meal instead of beef today
actions.description_ja: 今日は牛肉の代わりに植物性の食事を選択する
actions.description_es: Elegir un plato vegetal en vez de carne de vacuno hoy
actions.calculation_notes: per meal: a 100 g beef serving swapped for a plant alternative. Beef 70.3608 kg CO2e/kg, the production-weighted blend of the OWID / Poore & Nemecek 2018 means: 0.56 x 99.48 (beef herd) + 0.44 x 33.3 (dairy herd) = 70.36, with OWID's 56/44 beef-herd/dairy-herd production split; the same factor as the `beef` item in data/app/food_items.json. Per 100 g serving = 7036 g. Minus the standardized plant-alternative baseline of 200 g CO2e per 100 g serving (beans/lentils, OWID 'Other Pulses' mean 1.79 kg/kg = 179 g, rounded up to 200 g; the same baseline every meatless action uses) = 6836 g. Rounded down to 6800 g (savings always round DOWN). These are means including supply-chain losses; the ~60 kg/kg beef figure quoted elsewhere is the beef-herd median without losses (OWID FAQ below).

actions.calculation_notes: DENIM BASIS -- this value is a pair of jeans, not an average garment. Levi's own ISO 14040/14044 panel-reviewed LCA of the 501: 33.4 kg CO2e cradle-to-grave, of which consumer care is 37% and end of life 3%, both unavoidable whether the garment is new or secondhand. The production a buyer actually avoids is fibre 9% + fabric 27% + cut/sew/finish 8% + sundries and packaging 5% = 49% of 33.4 = 16.3 kg. Ships 15 kg, below that, on the same one-for-one displacement assumption as used_car_purchase (see notes.avoided_emissions_caveat). A cotton tee's production is several times lower, so this is generous for light garments. Next pass: source a light-garment LCA and bind to the minimum, as the food tier actions do.

notes.regional_variation: Energy-related actions vary significantly by grid carbon intensity. US average 0.37 kg/kWh, UK 0.21 kg/kWh, France 0.05 kg/kWh. Consider allowing user input.
notes.food_caveat: Transport accounts for only 5-6% of food emissions. 'Eat local' has limited impact compared to 'eat less beef'.
notes.reusable_items_caveat: Cotton bags require 7,100+ uses to break even. Recommend polypropylene bags (10-45 uses breakeven).
notes.growing_vegetables_caveat: University of Michigan 2024 found urban agriculture has 6× higher emissions than conventional farming due to infrastructure. Exception: tomatoes grown outdoors vs greenhouse.
notes.flight_radiative_forcing: DEFRA uses 1.9× multiplier for non-CO2 aviation effects. Some scientists argue 2.7-3× is more accurate.
notes.avoided_emissions_caveat: Actions that credit avoided manufacturing (used_car_purchase, secondhand_clothing, repair_item, borrow_instead_buy, donate_items) are COUNTERFACTUAL claims, not inventory accounting. Each scores one decision against what would otherwise have been produced; they are not a share of any physical object's embodied carbon. Two consequences. (1) They are not additive: if a car is built, sold, and resold, the manufacturing happened once, and crediting each buyer is only coherent because each buyer faced a separate buy-new decision -- never sum them and never present the total as a physical quantity of CO2 not emitted. (2) They assume one-for-one displacement, which is an upper bound: real markets displace less than one new unit per secondhand purchase, and no published rate exists to correct with. The methodology screen must say both.

Also the weaker of the pair on two counts: its 6 h/day of daylight substitution depends on season, latitude and window orientation, none of which the app knows, and its shipped value rested on a 40 W bulb that RESEARCH_ENERGY does not contain (section 3.5 ships an 8.5 W LED at 800 lm and a 60 W incandescent, nothing between). Retired value: 6 h x 40 W = 0.24 kWh x 458 g/kWh = 110, rounded down to 100. Restore only with a sourced fixture wattage and a daylight-availability basis.

ARCHIVED 2026-08-29 (owner call): no current definitive answer, so it stops shipping rather than shipping an unfounded number. The retired value was 300 g on the note 'avoids ~35% wasted energy/load' -- no factor, no arithmetic, no source, and the E1 grid rebase never touched it, so its basis is unknown and may predate the 458 g CO2e/kWh factor. The evidence base cannot supply a replacement: RESEARCH_ENERGY section 3.2 holds no partial-load washing measurement, because the Bosch WNA14400GR table that supplies all three wash temperatures is a max-load (9.0 kg) table only, and the dryer's half-load figure in the same section is a different appliance from the one this action names. The only '35%' in that document is the gas hob efficiency in section 3.4, unrelated to laundry -- a coincidence, not a lineage. Restore only with a measured partial-load figure for the same programme; the cheapest first check is whether the manufacturer documents already cited declare a half-load or quarter-load figure.

DEMOTED 2026-09-01 (recorded in PDR_FOOD_CALCULATOR.md section 6): shipped at 0 g since 2026-08-09 because the only peer-reviewed comparison runs the other way (Heard et al. 2019: delivered meal kits beat grocery-store meals, and last-mile emissions are lower for a van route than a car trip), so no primary supports a saving for cooking at home. A 0 g action still pays points at seed time (computed from effort/frequency/impact), so keeping it rewarded a habit the evidence cannot back -- the same honesty rule that retired use_natural_light.
